relationships.rationale: Capability-based organisation is the structural foundation for shifting from functional silos to customer-centric, end-to-end teams.
Customer-centricity requires teams to be measured on the customer outcomes they create, not on departmental output volumes.
End-to-end customer outcomes can only be designed for if processes are organised around the customer journey rather than departments.
Product teams are organised around capabilities and value streams, not the current org chart, so the capability map must be independent of organisational structure.
Full ownership of a value stream is only meaningful if the owning team is measured on the outcome that stream produces.
Full value-stream ownership requires the team to hold decision authority for the work within its stream, not escalate it elsewhere.
Decision authority sits with the team closest to the customer and the data, so evidence-based decisions are made where the evidence is freshest.
Citing evidence for every material decision depends on a continuous discovery practice that generates that evidence.
This strategy is the direct mandate for the continuous discovery principle — investment decisions follow evidence generated through ongoing discovery.
Quarterly investment rebalancing based on outcome evidence requires roadmaps to be framed as outcome hypotheses rather than fixed deliverable lists.
This strategy is the direct mandate for designing every new or redesigned process as fully digital end-to-end.
Digitising the top business processes end-to-end requires designing them around the customer journey they serve, not departmental boundaries.
This strategy is the direct mandate for sustainability metrics being owned by operating leaders rather than a separate reporting function.
Operational KPI dashboards including sustainability metrics by default is an instance of measuring teams on outcomes rather than output.
